claims.text: Applying a PECVD DLC coating with a Ti or Cr interlayer will significantly increase the surface hardness of high-performance tool steel relative to untreated steel.
Applying a PECVD DLC coating with a Ti or Cr interlayer will significantly reduce the friction coefficient of high-performance tool steel relative to untreated steel.
A thin Ti or Cr interlayer enhances adhesion between a DLC coating and a high-performance tool-steel substrate.
PECVD at 300–500 °C using methane or acetylene and controlled gas flows for several hours will produce a uniform, adherent DLC coating.
The deposited DLC will form an amorphous carbon network rich in sp3 bonds.
The Ti or Cr interlayer will provide robust, long-term adhesion of the DLC coating.
The DLC coating acts as an ultra-hard barrier over the underlying steel.
The DLC coating acts as a low-friction barrier over the underlying steel.
The DLC barrier protects the underlying steel from wear.
The DLC barrier protects the underlying steel from corrosion.
The coating protects the steel by absorbing mechanical impacts.
Reduced surface friction contributes to protection of the underlying steel.
The adhesion-promoting interlayer prevents premature delamination under cyclic mechanical or thermal stress.
Preventing delamination maintains the protective properties of the DLC coating.
The treated surface will have superior wear resistance under cyclic and abrasive loading relative to untreated tool steel.
The treated surface will have superior corrosion resistance in aggressive environments relative to untreated tool steel.
The benefits will remain effective during operation at 300–500 °C in typical aggressive environments encountered by high-value components.
Conditions beyond the stated temperature limits may require coating optimization or alternative treatments.
Published literature supports the effectiveness of DLC coatings.
